items.label: f02-check-order
items.front: RouteIQ's project check order, and what each step catches?
items.back: pnpm typecheck (sanitizer output vs DeliveryProof), pnpm lint (unsafe/unused code), pnpm test --run (behavior), pnpm build (Next.js App Router bundling boundary). Keep edits out of an active run; fix the first causal error.

items.label: f03-sanitizer-vs-guard
items.front: Sanitizer vs command guard: what is each, and what can a sanitizer never do?
items.back: A sanitizer projects a large unknown input space into a small accepted space; it cannot add a required timestamp or decide authorization. A command guard decides whether a state transition is allowed at all.

items.label: f01-delivery-invariant
items.front: RouteIQ: state the invariant a successful delivery mutation preserves, and why an invalid payload must not be 'fixed' into a partial event.
items.back: A successful delivery updates exactly one known stop and appends exactly one delivered event; an invalid stop or reason leaves state unchanged. A partially meaningful event would be counted by downstream summaries.

items.prompt: Why does RouteIQ silently drop a malformed delivery note but refuse an unknown failure reason outright?

choices.text: Notes are validated in the UI form, while reasons only reach the store
Dropping a reason would break TypeScript narrowing in setStopStatus
Unknown reasons exceed the localStorage budget, so they must be refused
The note is optional proof; the reason defines what the event means

choices: Notes are validated in the UI form, while reasons only reach the store
Dropping a reason would break TypeScript narrowing in setStopStatus
Unknown reasons exceed the localStorage budget, so they must be refused
The note is optional proof; the reason defines what the event means

items.explanation: 'Sanitization and rejection are separate policies.' Optional proof fields are sanitized away; recordFailure returns false for an unknown reason to avoid 'inventing a fake reason'. Inventing a reason would corrupt the reports.

items.explanation: The photo is trimmed and then must match /^data:image\/...;base64,...$/; other schemes are dropped, so the result is {} (the test asserts toEqual({})). Trimming does not rescue another URL scheme.

items.explanation: 'A good regression test asserts both the returned result and the absence of side effects for rejection... Avoid asserting implementation details such as helper call counts.'
